intro: Here, in the middle of Akhisar, an ancient city breathes. You are in Thyatira, in Manisa province, settled from the 3rd millennium BC until today. This is the ancient city at Akhisar, home to one of the Seven Churches of Revelation.
history: People have lived here since the 3rd millennium BC. The city was important in Lydian times, and under Rome it grew wealthy from its dye and textile industries. As one of the Seven Churches, Thyatira was the most important Roman city east of Smyrna.
structure-1: You are now at the Tepe Mezarı Remains. These are the remains of a burial chamber within a tumulus. Pause here for a moment, in a place made for the dead.
structure-3: Before you is the Early Church. These church remains date to the early centuries of Christianity, a quiet witness to the community that once gathered here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Colonnaded Street, then the Roman Bath, and finally the Basilica.
facts: Did you know? Thyatira was one of the seven churches of Revelation, and the city was famous for dyeing. Its name is linked to the region's famed dyeing industry, and its purple dye is celebrated in ancient sources. Lydia, the 'seller of purple' whom Paul met at Philippi in Acts, came from here. Today the ruins sit on an island of ground in the middle of modern Akhisar, ringed by apartment blocks.
outro: This brings our journey through Thyatira to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
